column1: # Label -> UBERON crosswalk for the TCIA Healthy-Total-Body-CTs collection (B2).
# Every `uberon` CURIE below was resolved by querying EBI OLS4 for the term and
# taking the exact match, not written from memory. Two guesses were wrong and are
# worth recording so nobody repeats them: the bone is `clavicle bone`
# (UBERON:0001105), because an exact search for "clavicle" returns *sternal end of
# clavicle* first; and "pelvis" resolves to RENAL pelvis, so the bony pelvis had
# to be searched for by name (UBERON:0001270).
# ⚠️ THE DEFINING PROPERTY OF THIS COLLECTION: LABELS ARE GROUPED.
# There is one `Ribcage`, not 24 ribs. One `Spine`, not 24 vertebrae. `Kidneys`,
# `Lung`, `Adrenal-glands` and every long bone merge left and right into a single
# mask. That is a property of the source, not of this table, and it cannot be
# refined here because the CT images are access-restricted so the data cannot be
# The consequence for this repo is specific: this atlas gives whole-body COVERAGE
# but not the per-structure identity ROADMAP Phase 1 exists to provide. Rows whose
# mask covers more than their term names carry status=flag, so `--strict` can drop
# them and the build reports them either way. The complement for granularity is the
# TotalSegmentator CT dataset, which has per-rib and per-vertebra labels and
# System assignments follow the precedent already set in
# `docs/moose-uberon-crosswalk.tsv` rather than being re-decided here -- including
# the spleen, which is flagged there for the same reason and gets the same note.
# ⚠️ THREE LABELS ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, AND THE NUMBERS ARE WHY.
# A first build kept them and produced a 403 MB asset of 15,190,538 triangles
# against a 380,000 target. Measured share of that total:
# They are diffuse tissue DEPOTS, not organs: enormous convoluted surface area,
# no anatomical boundary a viewer would look for, and the decimator's
# per-structure hole-avoidance back-off refuses to touch them (documented in
# docs/CT_ATLAS_PIPELINE.md as uneven decimation). D5a had already parked body
# composition as probably belonging to the SCORING path rather than the geometry
# path; this is the measurement that settles it for the geometry path.
# Their rows are kept below, commented out, so the mapping work is not lost and
# so re-enabling them is a one-character edit rather than a re-derivation.
# Columns match the MOOSE crosswalk so `read_crosswalk` needs no change.
# `moose_class` is the label name from the collection's own spreadsheet; the column
# keeps its name because the loader keys on it.

column9: note
Both glands in one mask. UBERON has per-side terms (0001234/0001233) but the mask cannot be split, so the unsided parent is the honest choice.
Urinary, not gall -- same reading as the MOOSE crosswalk.
⚠️ Low-dose non-contrast CT barely separates brain from CSF; treat the shape as indicative. The collection's own 37-119 labels are brain sub-structures and are absent from these files.
Whole heart, no chambers. The beating-heart overlay supersedes a chamber-level heart, not this one.
Both kidneys in one mask; UBERON's per-side terms (0004538/0004539) cannot be used.
⚠️ The pancreas is the organ non-contrast CT localises worst of all of these.

UBERON term is certain; the SYSTEM is a judgement call, and this repeats the MOOSE crosswalk's note verbatim in substance: the spleen is a lymphoid organ and the closed SystemId set has no lymphatic id. cardiovascular is the least-wrong home; metabolic is the other defensible answer.
Whole gland, not per-lobe.
VCI is vena cava inferior -- the spreadsheet's only abbreviated label.
Both lungs, no lobes. MOOSE segments five lobes; this is one mask.
All sixteen carpals, both wrists, one mask.
Both clavicles in one mask.
Both femora in one mask.
Both fibulae in one mask.
Both humeri in one mask.
All ten metacarpals in one mask.
All ten metatarsals in one mask.
Both patellae in one mask.
The BONY pelvis. An exact OLS4 search for "pelvis" returns renal pelvis, which is the trap here.
All twenty-eight phalanges of both hands. `manual digit` (UBERON:0002389) would be wrong -- that is the whole digit including soft tissue, and this mask is bone.
Both radii in one mask.
The rib cage as a structure, which is what the mask actually is. Individual ribs are not recoverable.
Both scapulae in one mask.

⚠️ PRIVACY. This is the structure the collection's own risk posture is inconsistent about: TCIA restricted the CT images citing facial reconstruction, then released the skull mask openly. Treat a rendered skull as identifying and see the defacing discussion in docs/CT_ATLAS_PIPELINE.md.
The column as a structure. C1-L5 are not separable, which is the single biggest loss against TotalSegmentator.
The bone HRA-male does not have at all.
All fourteen tarsals, both feet, one mask.
Both tibiae in one mask.
All phalanges of both feet. Bone, not `pedal digit`.
Both ulnae in one mask.
A TISSUE mask, not an organ -- every skeletal muscle in the field of view as one blob, with no individual muscle recoverable. It also OVERLAPS Psoas below, which is carved out of the same tissue.

Tissue, not organ, and the system is a judgement: subcutaneous fat sits under the skin, so integumentary is the least-wrong home in the closed set. D5a left body composition undecided between the geometry and scoring paths; this ships it as geometry and says so.

⚠️ THE WEAKEST ROW IN THIS TABLE. "Torso fat" has no UBERON equivalent. This is the standard counterpart to `subcutaneous adipose tissue` in body composition -- internal rather than under-skin fat -- so it is the closest term in kind, but it is narrower in extent: the mask covers the thorax too, and `abdominal` does not. `abdominal fat pad` (UBERON:0003427) was considered and is worse, being a discrete fat pad rather than the diffuse depot. Either get a reviewer to accept this or drop the label with --strict.
Both psoas muscles in one mask, and it overlaps Skeletal-muscle above -- the psoas IS skeletal muscle, so these two masks are not disjoint. Whichever is meshed second wins at the boundary.
